title: BETAPACE and BETAPACE AF (sotalol hydrochloride) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling (NDA019865), published in DailyMed; structured product labelling version 2, published 20 December 2024, label revised 6/2023
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement. The labeller submits the text and the Food and Drug Administration approves it.
result: Sotalol combines beta blockade (class II) with prolongation of the cardiac action potential (class III). Boxed warning, life-threatening proarrhythmia: sotalol can cause life-threatening ventricular tachycardia associated with QT prolongation; initiate or reinitiate it in a facility that can provide cardiac resuscitation and continuous electrocardiographic monitoring, hospitalise for at least 3 days, and reduce the dose, lengthen the interval or stop if QT reaches 500 ms or more; the dosing interval depends on creatinine clearance. Torsade de pointes risk rises with reduced creatinine clearance, female sex, higher doses, reduced heart rate and a history of sustained ventricular tachycardia, fibrillation or heart failure, and the QT effect and torsade risk are dose related. Sinus bradycardia below 50 beats per minute occurred in 13% of patients in trials and led to discontinuation in about 3%; sinus pause, arrest or node dysfunction in under 1%; second- or third-degree AV block in about 1%. It has not been shown to enhance survival in life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. In four placebo-controlled trials in atrial fibrillation or flutter, fatigue occurred in 20% and 19% at 160 to 240 and above 240 to 320 mg daily against 9% on placebo and bradycardia in 13% and 12% against 3%; 17% discontinued for adverse events, 10% within two weeks, including proarrhythmia in 2.2%. Other warnings: abrupt discontinuation, bronchospasm, masked hypoglycaemia, thyroid abnormalities, anaphylaxis and major surgery.
